title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX brings a PSP classic into a new era
summary: TOKYO, Japan – Konami is going back to Duel Academy with Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX, a remake of the 2008 PSP title Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Tag Force 3. Yu-Gi-Oh! has been enjoying something of a resurgence in…

blocks.text: TOKYO, Japan – Konami is going back to Duel Academy with Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX, a remake of the 2008 PSP title Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Tag Force 3.
Yu-Gi-Oh! has been enjoying something of a resurgence in recent years, from new games to the remaster of the Yu-Gi-Oh! GX anime.
Shown at Tokyo Game Show (TGS) 2026, Tag Force GX brings back the original’s mix of card battles, school life and relationship building, all centered around its signature Tag Duels.
Back to Duel Academy
The TGS demo starts with choosing from seven available partners, with Jaden Yuki among the options, before opening up Duel Academy to explore.
Students around the academy can be approached for conversations or challenged to either regular one-on-one matches or Tag Duels.
Naturally, it is the latter where Tag Force GX starts to distinguish itself.
Tag Duels pair the player and a chosen partner against another duo.
Teammates share their Life Points, field and Graveyard, meaning whatever one player does can potentially set up what their partner does next.
The format also makes getting into Yu-Gi-Oh! surprisingly approachable.
Partners can pick up some of the slack during easier encounters, giving returning players room to relearn the basics without immediately understanding every unfamiliar card.
Card information is readily accessible through a preview window as well, making it easy to check effects during a duel.

Building around your partner
There should be considerably more depth once deck building enters the equation.
Rather than simply building the strongest deck possible, players can find combinations that complement their partner’s strategy and potentially pull off increasingly elaborate plays together.
The short demo did not offer much time to explore deck building, but cards can be purchased from the in-game shop or even found scattered around Duel Academy.
Bringing the anime to life
Tag Force GX also embraces the spectacle that has always been part of the anime.
Signature monsters and attacks trigger animated sequences, while character portraits and voiced dialogue give duels some added personality.
Opponents can even pull off a dramatic Destiny Draw when a duel starts turning against them, while finishing attacks get their own flourish.
The visual upgrade is also immediately apparent compared with the game’s PSP origins.
It retains the smaller chibi-like characters while exploring Duel Academy, but models, portraits and duel animations have all received an overhaul.
More than just dueling
Outside of dueling, building relationships remains a major part of the experience.
Winning matches, giving gifts and participating in minigames strengthen affinity with a partner, eventually opening additional story events and alternate storylines for certain characters.
Konami says more than 100 characters will be available to interact and partner with in the full game, giving players plenty of options beyond the seven available during the TGS demo.
The remake also adds online multiplayer, something absent from the original Tag Force 3.
Free Match and Room Match modes will allow players to compete in regular and Tag Duels, with Room Matches supporting up to four players.
The TGS demo only offered a brief look at how everything comes together, but Tag Force GX feels more than simply an older Yu-Gi-Oh! game given a visual upgrade.
Its combination of Tag Duels, deck building and life at Duel Academy remains distinct, while the remake adds enough modern touches to bring the formula forward.
Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX launches Feb. 16, 2027, for Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC via Steam.
